policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV's main text says 'Israel be gathered unto him,' matching the qere/base ל֣וֹ ('unto him'); the mapped textual-variant note explicitly identifies 'Israel is not gathered' as another reading, distinguishing the ketiv alternative from the ASV text.

ASV's 'the preserved of Israel' does not distinguish the qere and ketiv spellings in this closed set, and the only mapped note is an alternative rendering about 'my salvation,' not a textual variant for this unit; both readings therefore remain compatible and the base fallback is retained.
ASV directly addresses the mountains with the plural imperative 'break forth into singing, O mountains,' distinguishing the qere/base imperative וּפִצְח֥וּ from the ketiv third-person form יפצחו.
